```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "asis")
r  <- params$report
d  <- r$days
s  <- r$settings
sl <- setNames(as.list(r$sleep$mean), r$sleep$var)
tm <- r$timing
ds <- r$daysum
dsm <- setNames(as.list(ds$mean), ds$var)
dom <- attr(ds, "domains")
coh <- r$coherence
dates <- range(d$date, na.rm = TRUE)
has_sleep <- r$n_nights > 0
has_diary <- r$n_diary > 0
note <- function(x) cat(sprintf('<p class="note">%s</p>', x))
```

<header class="hero">
<img class="logo" src="rth_logo.png" alt="Rise to Health, a Carnegie Mellon University study">
<h1>Your daily patterns</h1>
```{r}
cat(sprintf('<p class="dates">%s to %s &middot; %d diary days &middot; %d nights with the watch</p>',
            format(dates[1], "%B %d"), format(dates[2], "%B %d, %Y"), r$n_diary, r$n_nights))
```
</header>

<section class="intro">
<p><strong>Thank you for completing the daily assessments!</strong> For about two weeks you wore a sleep watch and told us about your days each night. This report puts those pieces together so you can see your own patterns.</p>
<p>Everything here describes <em>your</em> days only. It shows what tended to happen together, not what caused what. We are researchers, not medical doctors, so we can't give health advice or interpretations.</p>
</section>

<p class="cards-hint"><strong>Your overview.</strong> Each card sums up one section of this report; scroll down for the details. On a computer, you can click a card to jump to its section.</p>
<nav class="cards">
```{r}
tst_card <- if (has_sleep) fmt_hm(sl$tst) else "&mdash;"
bed_card <- if (has_sleep) tm$mean_clock[tm$var == "bed"] else "&mdash;"
cat(card("days", "Your events", fmt_num(dsm$stress_n), "unpleasant events a day"))
cat(card("mood", "Your mood", if (has_diary) sprintf("%s/100", round(dsm$pos_pomp)) else "&mdash;", "average positive mood"))
cat(card("sleep", "Sleep", tst_card, "average sleep a night"))
cat(card("sleep", "Sleep timing", bed_card, "average bedtime"))
cat(card("sleep-links", "Events &amp; sleep", sprintf("%d days", sum(!is.na(d$stress_n) & !is.na(d$tst))), "with a diary and sleep data"))
cat(card("mood-links", "Events &amp; mood", sprintf("%d days", sum(!is.na(d$stress_n) & !is.na(d$neg_pomp))), "with a diary"))
```
</nav>

<section id="days">
<h2>Your days</h2>
```{r}
if (!has_diary) {
  note("We didn't receive enough nightly diaries to show this section.")
} else {
  cat('<h3>Your events</h3>')
  cat("<p>Each night you told us what happened that day. Here's what a typical day looked like for you, and how much that changed from day to day.</p>")
  cat(events_glance_html(r))
  cat(sources_html(dom))
  cat('<h3 id="mood">Your mood</h3>')
  cat(sprintf("<p>You also rated how you felt each day. We put each mood on a 0 to 100 scale, where 0 is the lowest possible answer and 100 the highest. Your negative mood (like sad, worried, or lonely) averaged <strong>%s out of 100</strong>, and your positive mood (like happy, calm, or close to others) averaged <strong>%s out of 100</strong>.</p>",
              round(dsm$neg_pomp), round(dsm$pos_pomp)))
  cat(img_tag(plot_mood(d), height = 2.5, alt = "Daily mood"))
  if (isTRUE(r$trigger$triggered)) {
    cat('<div class="support-box"><p><strong>You told us that many of your days felt hard.</strong> That\'s worth paying attention to, and you don\'t have to handle it alone. Talking with someone you trust can help, and there are free, confidential resources you can reach any time.</p><p><a href="#support">See the support resources at the end of this report</a>.</p></div>')
  }
}
```
</section>

<section id="sleep">
<h2>Your sleep at a glance</h2>
```{r}
if (!has_sleep) {
  note("We didn't get usable sleep watch data for your nights, so this section is empty.")
} else {
  g <- r$guideline
  if (!is.null(g)) {
    cat(sprintf('<p>The National Sleep Foundation recommends <strong>%d to %d hours</strong> of sleep a night for people %s. Over your %d nights with the watch, you slept <strong>%s</strong> on average, ranging from %s to %s.</p>',
                g$lo, g$hi, g$group, r$n_nights, fmt_hm(sl$tst),
                fmt_hm(r$sleep$min[r$sleep$var == "tst"]), fmt_hm(r$sleep$max[r$sleep$var == "tst"])))
  }
  cat(glance_html(r))
}
```
</section>

<section id="nights">
<h2>Night to night fluctuations</h2>
```{r}
if (!has_sleep) {
  note("No sleep watch data to show here.")
} else {
  sd_tst <- r$sleep$sd[r$sleep$var == "tst"]
  cat(sprintf('<p>Sleep changes from night to night for everyone. Your sleep time usually landed within about <strong>%s</strong> of your average. This is called <em>sleep variability</em>: the smaller it is, the more regular your sleep.</p>',
              fmt_hm(sd_tst)))
  cat('<p class="hint">Dots are nights, the dashed line is your average, and shaded bands are the reference ranges from above.</p>')
  cat(img_tag(plot_nights(d, r$guideline, s$ref_se_min, s$ref_sol_max), height = 3.2, alt = "Sleep measures across nights"))
  mid_sd <- tm$sd_min[tm$var == "midpoint"]
  cat(sprintf('<p>Each bar below is one night, from getting into bed (top) to getting up (bottom).%s</p>',
              if (!is.na(mid_sd)) sprintf(' The middle of your sleep shifted by about <strong>%s</strong> from night to night.', fmt_hm(mid_sd)) else ""))
  cat('<p class="legend"><span class="sw sw-bed"></span>In bed <span class="sw sw-sleep"></span>Asleep</p>')
  cat(img_tag(plot_sleep_window_v(d, s$clock_anchor_h), height = 1.45, alt = "Time in bed and asleep each night"))
  cat(refs_html(c("Sleep regularity and mental health in teens (Castiglione-Fontanellaz et al., 2023)",
                  "https://doi.org/10.1111/jsr.13865")))
  cat('<p class="bridge">So what goes along with a longer or shorter night, or a calmer or harder day? The next two sections look at how your days, your mood, and your sleep moved together.</p>')
}
```
</section>

<section id="sleep-links">
<h2>How your events and that night&rsquo;s sleep went together</h2>
```{r}
sk <- r$sleep_links
n_pair_sleep <- sum(!is.na(d$stress_n) & !is.na(d$tst))
enough <- n_pair_sleep >= s$min_days
if (!enough) {
  note(sprintf("We need at least %d days with both a diary and a night of sleep watch data to look at these patterns, and we have %d from you.",
               s$min_days, n_pair_sleep))
}
if (enough) cat(events_sleep_html(r))
```
</section>

<section id="mood-links">
<h2>How your events and mood went together</h2>
```{r}
ml <- r$mood_links
n_pair_mood <- sum(!is.na(d$stress_n) & !is.na(d$neg_pomp))
if (n_pair_mood < s$min_days) {
  note(sprintf("We need at least %d diary days to look at these patterns, and we have %d from you. Thanks for the ones you did complete!",
               s$min_days, n_pair_mood))
}
ttl <- c(stress_n = "Unpleasant events", pos_n = "Positive events", help_n = "Helping others")
if (n_pair_mood >= s$min_days) {
  cat("<p>Each bar shows how your mood that day tended to differ on days with <strong>one more</strong> event. Bars inside the grey zone (less than 5 points out of 100 either way) we'd call &ldquo;about the same.&rdquo;</p>")
  cat(img_tag(plot_mood_change(ml, s$same_band[["neg_pomp"]]), height = 3.4,
              alt = "Change in mood on days with one more event"))
  cat('<div class="callout"><p><strong>What this can and can&rsquo;t tell you.</strong> These bars show what tended to happen <em>on the same day</em>, not what caused what, or which came first. Take helping others: if your negative mood tended to be lower on days you helped more, it could be that helping lifted your mood, that you were more likely to help when you were already in a good mood, or that something else about those days, like time with friends, made both more likely.</p></div>')
}
```
</section>

<section id="note">
<h2>A note on these numbers</h2>
<p>Everything in this report describes only your own days, about two weeks of them. We did not run statistical tests on your data alone, because a couple of weeks from one person isn't what those tests are designed for. So a pattern here is a description of what happened, not evidence that one thing affects another, and it might look different over a different two weeks.</p>
<p>That's where everyone's data come in. When we combine the diaries and sleep data from all the teens in Rise to Health, we have enough information to run statistical tests and ask questions like whether days with more unpleasant events tend to be followed by shorter sleep for teens in general, and which comes first. Those are the findings we'll share in our scientific publications. Stay tuned!</p>
</section>
